types.Person: An individual person named in the text, whatever their employer (such as researchers, accountants, technicians, engineers, officials, vendor representatives and residents); does not include teams, offices or other organizations.
types.Pump: A water pump unit or pumping assembly (such as station duty pumps or flume pumps); does not include non-pump scientific instruments, civil infrastructure, or tools.
types.Equipment: A non-pump mechanical device, scientific apparatus, tool, or component part (such as sediment flumes, soil corers, mechanical seals, and intake screens); does not include water pumps.
types.Place: A physical location, geographic site, station, room, street, or civil structure (such as Aldmoor bog, North Station, Mill Lane footbridge, Eastgate library, or room B12); does not include organizations or events.
types.Event: A time-bounded occurrence, scheduled activity, meeting, conference, talk, inspection round, failure incident, or municipal works project; does not include static places or continuous facilities.
types.Organization: A formal collective entity such as an institute team, municipal council, utility authority, or commercial vendor (such as Soil Ecology, Riverton Town Council, Riverton Water, or Calder Pumps); does not include individual persons or physical facilities.

institute/flume_commissioning.md#0.text:
# Flume commissioning notes

The sediment flume ran for the first time on 20 May 2025, at 40 litres per second, with Aiko Tanaka at the controls. Sand was fed at the upstream end and the bed formed ripples within an hour.

No run went above 60 litres per second in May: the committee had asked for a vibration measurement first.

institute/hensley_award.md#0.text:
# The Hensley Field-Work Award

The institute gives the Hensley Field-Work Award once a year for outstanding field work.

- 2022: Aiko Tanaka (Hydrology), for the river gauging survey.
- 2023: Jonathan Pike (Soil Ecology), for ten years of bog monitoring.
- 2024: not awarded. Samuel Osei was nominated, but the committee found that no entry met the standard.
- 2025: Maria Lopez (Soil Ecology), for the Aldmoor peat sampling campaign.

institute/minutes_2025-05-12.md#0.context: Minutes of the institute committee, 12 May 2025
institute/minutes_2025-05-12.md#0.text:
# Minutes of the institute committee, 12 May 2025

Present: Jon Pike (chair), Maria Lopez (Finance Office), Aiko Tanaka, Samuel Osei.

1. Budget. Maria Lopez presented the grants budget for 2025-26. The Aldmoor peat project is 18,000 euros over its equipment line; she asked the project lead to explain the overrun by the next meeting.

2. Reporting. Every project lead must submit a data management plan by 30 June 2025. Projects without a plan will not receive second-year funding.

3. Flume. Aiko Tanaka reported that the flume pump vibrates at high flow rates. Samuel Osei will measure the vibration before any experiment runs above 60 litres per second.

Jon Pike closed the meeting at 16:40.

institute/minutes_2025-06-09.md#0.context: Minutes of the institute committee, 9 June 2025
institute/minutes_2025-06-09.md#0.text:
# Minutes of the institute committee, 9 June 2025

Present: Aiko Tanaka (chair), Maria Lopez (Finance Office), J. Pike, Samuel Osei.

1. Aldmoor overrun. J. Pike explained the equipment overrun of the Aldmoor peat project: a second corer had to be bought after the first one jammed in December. The committee accepted the explanation.

2. Flume. Samuel Osei measured the flume pump vibration at 60 litres per second: 2.3 mm/s, below the 4.5 mm/s limit. Experiments above 60 litres per second may now start.

3. Travel. Maria Lopez reported that 60 percent of the 2025 travel budget has been spent.

Aiko Tanaka closed the meeting at 15:55.

institute/newsletter_spring_2025.md#0.text:
# Institute Newsletter, Spring 2025

## Field-work award

Maria Lopez of the Soil Ecology team received this year's Hensley Field-Work Award for her peat sampling campaign on the Aldmoor bog, where she collected 240 cores over two winters. Her group leader, Dr. Jonathan Pike, called the campaign "the most complete record of the bog we have".

## New hydrology flume

The Hydrology team, led by research engineer Aiko Tanaka, has finished building a 12-metre sediment flume in the basement laboratory. The first experiments start in May.

# Finance Office memo: travel claims

From: Maria Lopez, grants accountant

Travel claims for May must reach the Finance Office by 15 June 2025; later claims are paid in August. Please attach every receipt.

Several colleagues have asked how the June conference trips are funded. The trip of Maria Lopez (Soil Ecology) to the peat conference in Utrecht is charged to the Aldmoor peat project, as agreed with her group leader.

institute/utrecht_conference_2025.md#0.text:
# Back from Utrecht

Two of our researchers attended the European peat conference in Utrecht in June 2025. Maria Lopez presented a poster on the 240 cores of the Aldmoor bog, which drew more questions than any other poster in her session. Dr. Jonathan Pike chaired the session on peat as a carbon archive.

Next year's conference will be held in Tartu.

news/bakery_opens.md#0.text:
# New bakery on Harbour Street

Maria Lopez has opened a bakery at 14 Harbour Street, in the former post office. She trained in Valencia and bakes rye bread and pastries every morning from five.

"The street is full of potholes," she said. "I hope the resurfacing starts before winter, or my customers will stop coming."

news/budget_2025.md#0.text:
# Riverton sets its 2025 works budget

The council's works budget for 2025 lists five projects:

- Mill Lane footbridge repair: 180,000 pounds
- Eastgate library roof: 420,000 pounds
- Harbour Street resurfacing: 95,000 pounds
- Station Road drainage: 260,000 pounds
- Town hall boiler: 60,000 pounds

The contractor for the library roof must finish before the library reopens on 1 September. Councillor Priya Nandakumar asked for the drainage project to be moved ahead of the resurfacing; the vote on her motion was postponed.

news/budget_2026.md#0.text:
# Riverton's 2026 works budget published

The council has published its works budget for 2026. It lists five projects:

- Station Road drainage, second phase: 310,000 pounds
- Riverside path lighting: 230,000 pounds
- Eastgate library heating: 140,000 pounds
- Harbour Street resurfacing, carried over from 2025: 110,000 pounds
- Mill Lane footbridge east railing: 15,000 pounds

Councillor Priya Nandakumar welcomed the second drainage phase but asked why the resurfacing had slipped by a year.

news/council_notices.md#0.text:
# Council notices

Mill Lane footbridge: closed to all users from 3 February for repair works, for about eight weeks.

Harbour Street: resurfacing postponed to 2026. The street stays open to traffic.

Station Road: lane closures from September while the drainage is rebuilt.

news/flood_meeting.md#0.context: Public meeting on Station Road flooding
news/flood_meeting.md#0.text:
# Public meeting on Station Road flooding

About eighty residents came to the town hall on Thursday to discuss the flooding of Station Road.

Dr Jonathan Pike of the environmental institute explained how the peat bogs upstream hold back rain and slow the flow into the river. The council's structural inspector, Daniel Okafor, said the culvert under Station Road is too narrow for heavy storms.

Mayor Helen Achterberg said the drainage works will start in September. Councillor Priya Nandakumar repeated her call to move them ahead of the Harbour Street resurfacing.

news/footbridge_reopens.md#0.text:
# Mill Lane footbridge reopens

The Mill Lane footbridge reopened on 28 March after eight weeks of works. Both railings and all 46 deck boards were replaced. Mayor Achterberg thanked residents for their patience and said the works had come in 12,000 pounds under budget.

news/harbour_open_day.md#0.text:
# Riverton Water opens its doors

Harbour Station welcomed some sixty visitors at Riverton Water's open day on Saturday. Technician Rosa Delgado showed them the station's Kestrel V-12 pump and explained how the alarms reach North Station when the site is unmanned.

Children could try a hand pump in the yard, and the café sold out of cakes by noon.

news/letter_to_the_editor.md#0.text:
# Letter: the footbridge is not safe

Sir, the mayor tells us the Mill Lane footbridge is safe to use. I cross it every morning with my daughter, and the east railing still moves when you lean on it. Nobody has fixed it, and no warning sign has been put up.

Gareth Lowe, Mill Lane

news/mill_lane_and_eastgate.md#0.text:
# Council votes on two repairs

The Riverton town council voted 7 to 2 on Tuesday to repair the Mill Lane footbridge and to replace the roof of the Eastgate library.

The footbridge will be closed from 3 February while its railings and deck boards are renewed. The library roof, which has leaked into the children's section since the autumn storms, will be replaced over the summer, when the library closes for four weeks.

Mayor Helen Achterberg said the footbridge "is safe to use until the works begin". The council's structural inspector, Daniel Okafor, wrote in his report that residents had told him the east railing moved when leaned on; he recommended closing the bridge at once.

# Calder Pumps: quotation for seal kits

Dear Riverton Water,

Following the seal failure on one of your North Station pumps in March, we are pleased to quote for spare seal kits.

In our experience a Hydra P-40 needs a new mechanical seal every 18 months of duty. We therefore recommend keeping two reconditioned seal kits in stock, at 640 euros each, delivery within ten working days.

Kind regards,
Ines Barros, Service Manager, Calder Pumps

water/harbour_station_may_2025.md#0.text:
# Harbour Station monthly report, May 2025

The station's only pump, KV12-0457, tripped three times in the first week of May on low suction pressure. On 6 May Rosa Delgado found the intake screen half blocked with leaves and cleaned it. No trip has occurred since.

Average flow for the month was 17 litres per second. The station was unmanned for the rest of May, with alarms routed to North Station.

water/incident_2025-03-29.md#0.context: Incident report: flooding of the North Station dry well
water/incident_2025-03-29.md#0.text:
# Incident report: flooding of the North Station dry well

On 29 March 2025 the mechanical seal of pump HP40-1183 failed during the night shift. About 3,000 litres of water flooded the dry well before the operator isolated the pump. Flow on the North main dropped to 31 litres per second until HP40-2291 was switched to duty.

Site engineer Tomasz Wren wrote that the flooding would have been avoided had the seal been replaced after the March inspection, as the inspection had recommended.

The seal of HP40-1183 was replaced on 31 March 2025 by technician Rosa Delgado.

water/inspection_2025-03-14.md#0.text:
# North Station pump inspection, 14 March 2025

Technician Rosa Delgado inspected both Hydra P-40 pumps at North Station during the quarterly round.

Pump HP40-1183 showed a slow drip from the mechanical seal and a bearing temperature of 71 °C, above the 65 °C alarm limit. Delgado tagged it for a seal replacement within two weeks.

Pump HP40-2291 ran quietly. No leaks were found on HP40-2291, and its bearing temperature was 48 °C.

Measured flow: HP40-1183 delivered 38 litres per second, HP40-2291 delivered 41 litres per second.

water/inspection_2025-06-13.md#0.text:
# North Station pump inspection, 13 June 2025

Technician Rosa Delgado carried out the summer quarterly round on the two Hydra P-40 pumps at North Station.

Pump HP40-2291 now shows a slow drip from its mechanical seal, and its bearing temperature has risen to 52 °C. Delgado tagged HP40-2291 for a seal change before the end of the month.

Pump HP40-1183, with the seal fitted on 31 March, was dry: no leaks were found on HP40-1183, and its bearing temperature was 49 °C.

Measured flow: HP40-1183 delivered 40 litres per second, HP40-2291 delivered 39 litres per second.

water/isolation_procedure.md#0.text:
## Contents

1. Before you start
2. Isolating a duty pump

# Isolating a pump at North Station

Written by Tomasz Wren for new operators.

## Before you start

Tell the control room which pump you will isolate, and check that the standby pump is available.

## Isolating a duty pump

Switch the standby pump to duty first. Then stop the pump you are isolating, close its discharge valve, and close its suction valve last. Lock both valves and hang a tag on the starter.

water/north_station_2024_summary.md#0.text:
# North Station: summary of 2024

North Station pumped 1.9 million cubic metres in 2024. HP40-1183 ran for 6,100 hours and HP40-2291 for 2,300 hours, as HP40-1183 was kept on duty for most of the year.

No seal failures were recorded in 2024. The only stoppage was a four-hour power cut on 17 November, when both pumps were off.

For 2025 the site engineer, Tomasz Wren, plans to share the duty more evenly between the two pumps.

water/shift_notes.txt#0.text:
Shift notes, North Station, week of 7 April 2025.
Mon: HP40-2291 on duty all week, flow steady at 41 l/s.
Tue: Calder Pumps phoned about the seal returned from HP40-1183. Their service manager, Ines Barros, said the pump had run dry and that the warranty does not cover the seal. Our log shows the suction valve open for the whole night of the failure, so we do not accept that the pump ran dry.
Wed: the Kestrel V-12 at Harbour Station (serial KV12-0457) tripped twice on low suction pressure; reset both times, no damage found.
Thu: nothing to report.

water/shift_notes_june.txt#0.text:
Shift notes, North Station, week of 9 June 2025.
Mon: HP40-1183 on duty, flow steady at 40 l/s; HP40-2291 on standby.
Tue: alarm from Harbour Station at 03:10, cleared remotely; KV12-0457 restarted on its own.
Wed: Tomasz Wren visited to plan the seal change on HP40-2291 and asked for the old seal to be kept.
Thu: nothing to report.
Fri: quarterly inspection by Rosa Delgado.

water/work_orders_2025-06.md#0.text:
# Work orders, North Station, June 2025

WO-311, 2 June. Bearings of HP40-1183 regreased by Rosa Delgado. Pump returned to duty the same day.

WO-318, 30 June. Mechanical seal of HP40-2291 replaced by technician Marek Hollis, following the tag from the June inspection. The old seal was kept for the vendor.

WO-320, 30 June. Test run of HP40-2291 after the seal change: 41 litres per second, no leaks, bearing temperature 47 °C.
